recent_posts.title: Animated icons for React, without the setup pain
recent_posts.summary: @animateicons/react is a new npm package providing animated Lucide-style icons for React applications. It aims to simplify adding motion details to buttons, menus, dashboards, and landing pages without building custom SVG animations from scratch. Installation is via pnpm/npm and icons are imported directly from the package with size and color props.

recent_posts.title: The Complete Guide to Location Indexing: Geohash, Quadtree, Google S2, and Uber H3
recent_posts.summary: A comparison of four location indexing strategies used by major tech companies to solve the performance problem of 2D geospatial queries on large datasets. Covers Geohash (Yelp), Quadtree (Twitter), Google S2, and Uber H3, explaining the tradeoffs each approach makes. Includes a practical rule for choosing cell size relative to search radius to avoid silent correctness bugs at scale.

recent_posts.title: Circuit Breaker Explained
recent_posts.summary: A real-world incident postmortem where a single slow payment service triggered a cascading failure across six unrelated services in under two minutes. The root cause was retry logic without circuit breakers — each of 12 upstream callers retried 3 times with backoff, multiplying load 4x and creating a self-inflicted DDoS. The fix: wrap every outbound call in a circuit breaker (opossum for Node.js, resilience4j for Java), only allow retries inside a closed circuit with jitter, and cap retry budgets per request chain. The key principle: circuit breaker first, retry inside it — never retry through an open circuit.

recent_posts.title: Bridging Backend and DevOps: Managing Kubernetes-Native Abstractions
recent_posts.summary: Backend engineers using Go and Spring Boot face operational challenges beyond writing business logic, particularly around connecting internal developer platforms to Kubernetes deployments. Teams building DIY platforms with Backstage need deployment abstractions that let backend teams deploy autonomously while DevOps retains governance. OpenChoreo, an open-source project approaching v1.0 and CNCF Sandbox status, is presented as a solution for managing Kubernetes-native workloads and integrating with platform engineering ecosystems.

recent_posts.title: AWS Lambda Architecture
recent_posts.summary: Most engineers use AWS Lambda without understanding its internals. Three key questions reveal common knowledge gaps: Lambda runs on Firecracker microVMs (not containers), the second invocation is faster because execution environments are cached (so global-scope initialization matters), and account-level concurrency is a shared regional pool meaning one misbehaving function can throttle all others. Understanding these internals explains cold start behavior and unexpected throttling incidents.

recent_posts.title: Push VS Poll
recent_posts.summary: A practical framework comparing push vs pull communication patterns in distributed systems across five dimensions: consumer control (backpressure), latency, failure modes, fan-out scaling, and infrastructure cost. Covers real-world tool choices like webhooks vs Kafka and StatsD vs Prometheus, with decision criteria for when to use each pattern. Concludes that most production systems use a hybrid approach where CDC pushes to Kafka and consumers pull from it.

recent_posts.title: AWS Lambda Aliases & Versions
recent_posts.summary: AWS Lambda Versions and Aliases are often overlooked features that enable safe, zero-downtime deployments. Versions are immutable snapshots of function code and config, while Aliases act as named pointers to specific versions. The key capability is weighted traffic routing, which enables true canary deployments — e.g., sending 90% of traffic to v5 and 10% to v6 — without infrastructure changes. A recommended pattern uses $LATEST only for dev/testing, immutable tagged versions for releases, and aliases like 'prod' and 'canary' for traffic control. Pointing production directly at $LATEST removes rollback capability and risks silent incidents.

recent_posts.title: The Outbox Pattern
recent_posts.summary: The dual write problem occurs when saving to a database and publishing to a message broker are two separate non-atomic operations — a crash between them leaves your systems permanently out of sync. The Outbox Pattern solves this by inserting the event into an outbox table within the same database transaction as the business write, then using a separate publisher process (polling or CDC via Debezium) to relay events to the broker. This guarantees atomicity at the write side, but delivers at-least-once semantics, meaning consumers must be idempotent. Distributed transactions (2PC) are not a viable alternative for event-driven systems. The pattern is used in production by Shopify and is a first-class feature in Dapr.

recent_posts.title: AWS Lambda Powertools
recent_posts.summary: Duplicates are a guaranteed property of distributed systems on AWS — SQS retries, API Gateway client retries, EventBridge retries, and Lambda async retries all produce them. AWS Lambda Powertools' idempotency utility solves this using DynamoDB as a persistence layer with a single Python decorator. The flow extracts an idempotency key via JMESPath, uses conditional writes to track IN_PROGRESS and COMPLETED states, and returns cached results for duplicate events. Common mistakes include using Lambda's requestId or SQS receiptHandle as keys. The right approach is combining business identity fields like merchant_id and client_request_id, with TTL set to match the retry window (24 hours to 7 days for payments).

recent_posts.title: DynamoDB Indexes GSI VS LSI
recent_posts.summary: A practical breakdown of DynamoDB's two index types — Local Secondary Index (LSI) and Global Secondary Index (GSI) — covering their key differences, hidden pitfalls, and when to use each. LSIs must be created at table creation time, support strongly consistent reads, but have a hard 10 GB per-partition limit that can silently cause write failures. GSIs can be added anytime and have no size limit, but only support eventual consistency and can throttle the base table if their write capacity is under-provisioned. AWS itself recommends GSIs in most cases. A decision framework is provided to guide the choice based on access patterns, consistency requirements, and data growth expectations.

top_posts.summary: Learn how RabbitMQ can help decouple microservices, handle asynchronous tasks, and build resilient systems. The tutorial covers setting up RabbitMQ with Docker and creating producers and receivers to eliminate bottlenecks in your backend architecture.

top_posts.title: Database less OTP- A concept
top_posts.summary: The post explains how an OTP system typically works and proposes a concept for a database-less OTP system using hashing and JSON Web Tokens (JWT) to reduce costs. It suggests creating a raw OTP sent to the user and a corresponding hashed OTP shared with the user's browser. This approach can prevent database dependency while maintaining security. A demo and GitHub repositories for the backend and frontend implementations are provided.
